meta.name: Bridger POPLAR-RICHEY 10.75in - Pack-and-Coast (1.3 MMscf budget), 2.5 mph cap [RECOMMENDED]
meta.notes: Bridger POPLAR -> RICHEY nitrogen purge. 10.75" OD x 0.219" WT uniform, 25.97 mi (KMZ traced route), Richland/Dawson Co. MT. Pig launches at the NORTH (Poplar) end and runs SOUTH; crude exits the south end into tankage. Net elevation gain +519 ft (2336 ft launch -> 2855 ft receipt) with rolling terrain to ~MP 18 and a steady 8-mile climb from MP 18 to the receipt. Fluid: light sweet crude (ASSUMED API ~40 / SG 0.82 / 3.5 cSt - CONFIRM). Tankage receipt held at 50 psig min. MOP envelope = 1440 psig (ANSI 600) flat - no pipe grade / hydro / PxP data supplied; Barlow at 0.72 design factor needs >= X52 to justify 1440 (X42 would be ~1230 psig). HARD 2.5 mph pig speed cap. Single N2 injection at the launch trap - no boosters, no pump stations, no BPCV. KEY FINDING: this line is SPEED-capped, not drive-capped. Holding 2.5 mph needs only ~490 psig at the pig face (184 psi static lift + ~230 psi crude friction + 50 psi receipt), roughly a third of the 1440 MOP, so any additional drive pressure is pure wasted nitrogen packed into the line. Zero MOP violations at every drive level tested (0.3-0.9 x 1440); the net-uphill profile means there is no downhill static-head overpressure of downstream joints (unlike THUNDERBIRD). STRATEGY: PACK-AND-COAST. One continuous nitrogen injection at ~4,570 SCFM / ~490 psig for the first 4.7 hr (pig MP 0 -> 11.8), then ONE cut and coast the remaining 14.2 mi on the stored compressed column. Result: 1.31 MMscf, 10.36 hr, a FLAT 2.5 mph the entire run (no dip anywhere), 0 MOP violations, 0 vent, arrival pig face ~217 psig. 1.3 MMscf is the leanest budget with NO speed penalty - 1.2M dips to 2.05 mph, 1.1M to 1.5 mph, 1.0M to 0.64 mph, and 0.9M stalls at MP 17. Pack pressure is essentially irrelevant here (0.35 to 0.70 x MOP all give identical results) because the controller throttles injection to the minimum face needed for target speed; the BUDGET alone sets the cut point. 0.35 x 1440 = 504 psig is used as the pack target because it is the lowest setting that never limits speed off the launch - it keeps peak line pressure under 500 psig, which cuts the compression spec and the end-of-job blowdown volume.
